summary_en: Mitsui E&S agreed to sell its entire 51.06% stake (844,546 shares) in subsidiary Kaji Tech to CSRI 17 K.K. through a tender offer followed by share consolidation and Kaji Tech's self-repurchase. The transaction eliminates parent-subsidiary dual listing and allows Kaji Tech greater operational independence for growth initiatives.
title_en: Notice of Conclusion of Tender Offer Agreement for Shares of Subsidiary (Kaji Tech Co., Ltd.) and Planned Change in Consolidated Subsidiaries
translation_en_brief:
On November 10, 2026, Mitsui E&S Holdings announced its agreement with CSRI 17 K.K. to sell all 844,546 shares it owns in Kaji Tech Co., Ltd., representing 51.06% of the subsidiary's outstanding shares. The transaction will be executed through a public tender offer for Kaji Tech shares, followed by share consolidation to make Mitsui E&S and CSRI 17 K.K. the only shareholders, and then Kaji Tech's self-repurchase of all shares held by Mitsui E&S. Upon completion of the share consolidation, Kaji Tech will cease to be a consolidated subsidiary of Mitsui E&S.

The company stated that eliminating the parent-subsidiary dual-listing structure will remove potential conflicts of interest and allow Kaji Tech to independently execute growth strategies including personnel investment, overseas expansion, and M&A more flexibly. Simultaneously, Mitsui E&S will concentrate management resources on strengthening its core maritime propulsion systems and logistics businesses. The price was structured to generate tax benefits under Japan's corporate income tax rules governing deemed dividends, such that Mitsui E&S's after-tax proceeds from the self-repurchase mechanism will be equivalent to what it would receive if it tendered its shares at the public offer price, ensuring fair treatment compared to other Kaji Tech shareholders.
